foods.name: Doenjang (Korean Fermented Soybean Paste)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Long-fermented soybean paste similar to miso. Very high biogenic amines.

foods.name: Citrus (Mixed: Orange, Lemon, Lime, Grapefruit)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2 as histamine liberator. Citrus triggers mast cell degranulation independent of histamine content. High salicylates.

foods.name: Pineapple (Canned)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Canned = higher histamine than fresh. Bromelain is also a histamine liberator.

foods.name: Papaya (Green/Unripe)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Papain enzyme is a histamine liberator. Less ripe = lower overall but still triggers mast cells.

foods.name: Strawberry (Frozen)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Histamine liberator. Frozen storage increases histamine slightly. Very high salicylates (RPAH).

foods.name: Tomato Sauce (Cooked/Concentrated)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Cooking concentrates histamine. Tomato is both high-histamine and a histamine liberator. Triple threat: content + liberation + cooking concentration.

foods.name: Black Tea (Strong Brew)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1 content but DAO inhibitor. Catechins block diamine oxidase enzyme. Combined effect with histamine-containing meals is synergistic. Very high oxalates.

foods.name: Green Tea (Strong Brew)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1, DAO inhibitor. EGCG catechins block DAO. High oxalates. Salicylate content moderate (RPAH).

foods.name: Energy Drink (Monster/Rockstar)
foods.source_notes: DAO inhibitor via caffeine content. High fructose corn syrup base. Taurine and B-vitamins may also affect histamine metabolism in sensitive individuals.

foods.name: Alcohol (Spirits, Clear - Vodka/Gin)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Alcohol is a potent DAO inhibitor regardless of histamine content. Clear spirits have less histamine than wine/beer but still block DAO. Distilled spirits generally gluten-safe.

foods.name: Alcohol (Whiskey/Bourbon)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Barrel aging adds histamine and amines. DAO inhibitor. Salicylates from oak barrel aging.

foods.name: Leftover Meat (24hr Refrigerated)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI guidance: histamine in cooked meat approximately doubles every 24hr at fridge temp. 24hr leftovers = moderate risk.

foods.name: Leftover Fish (24hr Refrigerated)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI guidance: fish accumulates histamine faster than other meats. 24hr leftover fish is HIGH risk. Freeze immediately after cooking if not eating within 2hr.

foods.name: Leftover Meat (48hr+ Refrigerated)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI guidance: 48hr+ leftovers = high histamine. Critical MCAS guidance: freeze within 2hr of cooking, thaw and eat same day.

foods.name: Bone Broth (Short Simmer, <4hr)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Shorter simmering = less histamine extraction. Still moderate due to collagen breakdown. Better option than 24hr bone broth for MCAS patients.

foods.name: Bone Broth (Long Simmer, 12-24hr)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2-3. Extended simmering extracts and generates high histamine from protein breakdown. The 'healthy bone broth' trend is an MCAS trap.

foods.name: Rejuvelac
foods.source_notes: Fermented wheat/grain water. High histamine from fermentation. Contains gluten unless made with quinoa/rice.

foods.name: Apple Cider Vinegar (Unpasteurized)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Unpasteurized 'with mother' = active fermentation = high histamine. Popular health trend problematic for MCAS/HIT.

foods.name: Yogurt (Flavored, Commercial)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Fermented dairy has moderate histamine. Flavored versions add fructose syrup and fruit (salicylates). Lactose varies by brand.

foods.name: Sour Cream (Full Fat)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1. Cultured dairy product. Moderate histamine from bacterial fermentation. Lower than aged cheese.

foods.name: Buttermilk (Cultured)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1. Cultured dairy. Moderate histamine. High lactose content.

foods.name: Cinnamon (High Dose/Supplement)
foods.source_notes: RPAH very high salicylates. Cinnamon is a known mast cell trigger at higher doses. MCAS patients frequently report reactions.

foods.name: Artificial Food Coloring (Red 40, Yellow 5/6)
foods.source_notes: Known mast cell degranulation triggers. RPAH elimination diet excludes all artificial colors. Tartrazine (Yellow 5) particularly problematic for aspirin-sensitive patients.

foods.name: MSG (Monosodium Glutamate)
foods.source_notes: Glutamate is structurally similar to histamine. RPAH lists as amine. Controversial in general population but well-documented trigger in MCAS patients.

foods.name: Sulfites (Wine/Dried Fruit Preservative)
foods.source_notes: FDA-recognized allergen (required labeling >10ppm). Triggers mast cell degranulation. Common in wine, dried fruits, shrimp, processed meats. Cross-reactive with aspirin sensitivity.

foods.name: Sodium Benzoate (Preservative)
foods.source_notes: RPAH elimination diet excludes benzoates. Structurally related to salicylates. Known mast cell trigger. Found in soft drinks, pickles, sauces.

foods.name: Sausage (Bratwurst)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Fresh sausage (not dry-cured) still has moderate-high histamine from processing. Spice blend adds salicylates.

foods.name: Italian Sausage (Sweet/Hot)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Fennel, paprika, chili flakes add salicylates. Garlic/onion in fructans. Often contains wine (histamine).

foods.name: Nduja (Spreadable Salami)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Fermented spreadable salami with Calabrian chili. Peak histamine + very high salicylates from chili.

foods.name: Coppa (Capocollo)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Dry-cured pork neck/shoulder. 3-6 month curing = very high biogenic amines.

foods.name: Pancetta
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2-3. Italian cured pork belly. Less aged than prosciutto but still high histamine from salt-curing.

foods.name: Sopressata
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Dry-cured Italian salami with chili flakes. Very high biogenic amines from extended fermentation.

foods.name: Dried Apricots (Sulfured)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Sulfite preservation triggers mast cells. Concentration of salicylates from drying. Monash high FODMAP in fructose and polyols.

foods.name: Dried Cranberries (Craisins)
foods.source_notes: RPAH high salicylates. Often sulfured (check label). Added sugar concentrates fructose. Oxalates moderate.

foods.name: Dried Mango
foods.source_notes: RPAH high salicylates. Concentration from drying. Often sulfured. Very high fructose from Monash data.

foods.name: Dates (Medjool)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 histamine. Monash very high FODMAP (fructose). Low histamine but high fructose load.

foods.name: Coconut Aminos (Soy Sauce Alternative)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0-1. Fermented coconut sap. Much lower histamine than soy sauce. Common MCAS-friendly soy sauce substitute. Some polyols from coconut.

foods.name: Fresh Chicken (Cooked Immediately)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Fresh meat cooked immediately and eaten fresh = minimal histamine. Key MCAS guidance: buy fresh, cook same day, eat immediately or freeze.

foods.name: Fresh Beef (Cooked Immediately)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Fresh beef cooked immediately. Slightly higher baseline than chicken but still very low when fresh.

foods.name: Fresh Salmon (Cooked Immediately)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when truly fresh. Fish degrades fastest of all proteins. MCAS guidance: buy same-day catch, cook within hours. Flash-frozen at sea is often safer than 'fresh' display case fish.

foods.name: Cream Cheese (Fresh, Not Aged)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Fresh unaged cheese = very low histamine. One of the safer dairy options for histamine-sensitive patients. Lactose still present.

foods.name: Mozzarella (Fresh)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Fresh mozzarella (not low-moisture pizza cheese) = very low histamine. Histamine-friendly dairy option.

foods.name: Sourdough Bread
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Fermentation produces histamine. Paradoxically, long fermentation reduces FODMAP fructans vs commercial bread. Gluten still present.

foods.name: Miso Soup (Restaurant)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2-3. Miso paste + dashi (dried bonito = high histamine) + often seaweed (nickel). Restaurant version typically uses longer-fermented miso.

foods.name: Olives (Cured/Brined)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Brining/curing adds moderate histamine. Olives are among highest salicylate foods (RPAH). Double concern for MCAS.

foods.name: Capers
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Salt/vinegar cured flower buds. Extremely high salicylates (RPAH). Quercetin-rich (a natural antihistamine paradox but salicylate load dominates for MCAS).

foods.name: Sun-Dried Tomatoes (Oil-Packed)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Concentration from drying dramatically increases histamine, salicylates, oxalates. Oil packing adds to shelf life but doesn't reduce histamine. Triple-high food.

foods.name: Shrimp (Frozen, Thawed)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Shellfish is a known histamine liberator. Frozen shrimp starts moderate; thawing time is critical. Cook immediately after thaw.

foods.name: Sushi (Raw Fish, Restaurant)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2-3. Raw fish histamine depends entirely on freshness/handling. Restaurant sushi quality varies. Soy sauce (high histamine) + wasabi (salicylates) + rice vinegar all add load. Gluten from soy sauce.

foods.name: Chocolate Milk
foods.source_notes: Cocoa is a histamine liberator + DAO inhibitor (SIGHI 2). Combined with high-lactose milk. Oxalates from cocoa.

foods.name: Protein Powder (Plant-Based Blend)
foods.source_notes: Pea/rice/hemp blend. Generally low histamine. GOS from pea protein. Lectins from legume base. Check for soy-derived ingredients.

foods.name: Electrolyte Powder (LMNT/Liquid IV)
foods.source_notes: Generally MCAS-safe. Check for citric acid (histamine liberator), stevia (salicylates), artificial flavors/colors. LMNT is clean; Liquid IV has more additives.

foods.name: Kvass
foods.source_notes: Fermented rye bread beverage. High histamine from fermentation. Contains gluten from rye.

foods.name: Water Kefir
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Fermented sugar water with kefir grains. Less histamine than dairy kefir or kombucha but still moderate from fermentation.

foods.name: Tepache
foods.source_notes: Mexican fermented pineapple beverage. Moderate histamine from fermentation. Bromelain (histamine liberator) from pineapple.

foods.name: Cinnamon Roll (Commercial)
foods.source_notes: Cinnamon is very high salicylates (RPAH). Combined with wheat gluten, dairy, fructose syrup. A multi-trigger food that seems innocent.

foods.name: Rotisserie Chicken (Store-Bought)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Store rotisserie sits in warming case for hours = histamine accumulation. Seasoning blends often contain MSG, paprika (salicylates). Better than deli meat but worse than fresh-cooked.

foods.name: Deli Roast Beef
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. Processed deli meat. Extended refrigeration display = histamine accumulation. Preservatives add load.

foods.name: Turkey Sausage
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2. 'Healthy' alternative to pork sausage still has histamine from processing. Often contains fillers and spice blends.

foods.name: Chicken Sausage (Pre-Cooked)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Pre-cooked links like Aidells. Lower histamine than cured sausage but still moderate from processing. Often contains garlic (fructans).

foods.name: Whole Milk
foods.source_notes: Monash very high FODMAP lactose. SIGHI 0 histamine. Primary dairy allergen (casein + whey). Full fat slightly better tolerated GI than skim.

foods.name: Skim Milk (Fat-Free)
foods.source_notes: Monash very high FODMAP lactose. Slightly higher lactose concentration than whole milk due to fat removal. Same allergen profile (casein + whey).

foods.name: Half and Half
foods.source_notes: ~12% fat mix of milk and cream. Less lactose than whole milk but still high. Small serving may be tolerated.

foods.name: Evaporated Milk
foods.source_notes: Concentrated milk with 60% water removed. Very high lactose concentration. Heat processing slightly increases histamine/amines.

foods.name: Condensed Milk (Sweetened)
foods.source_notes: Concentrated milk + ~45% added sugar. Extremely high lactose + fructose from added sucrose.

foods.name: All-Purpose Wheat Flour
foods.source_notes: Monash high FODMAP fructans. ~10-12% gluten. WGA lectin present. Core ingredient in most baked goods.

foods.name: Wheat Bread (White, Sliced)
foods.source_notes: Monash high FODMAP fructans (2 slices). Standard commercial bread. Most contain soy lecithin, DATEM, and other additives.

foods.name: Semolina
foods.source_notes: Durum wheat flour. Very high gluten. Used in pasta, couscous, Middle Eastern desserts.

foods.name: Bulgur Wheat
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP fructans at typical serving. Parboiled cracked wheat. Slightly better tolerated FODMAP than raw wheat flour.

foods.name: Tofu (Firm)
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP in firm varieties (GOS washed out in pressing). Soy lectin moderate. Nickel accumulator. SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Silken Tofu
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP GOS (less pressing than firm). Higher GOS than firm tofu. Soy allergen present.

foods.name: Cashews (Raw)
foods.source_notes: Monash high FODMAP GOS. Tree nut allergen (Anacardiaceae family, cross-reacts with pistachio and mango). Moderate oxalates and nickel.

foods.name: Macadamia Nuts (Raw)
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP in reasonable serving. One of the better-tolerated tree nuts. Tree nut allergen (Proteaceae family). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Hazelnuts (Filberts)
foods.source_notes: Tree nut allergen (Betulaceae family). Cross-reacts with birch pollen (OAS). Moderate salicylates. Used in Nutella.

foods.name: Pecans (Raw)
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP polyols at larger serving. Tree nut allergen (Juglandaceae family, cross-reacts with walnut). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Crawfish (Crayfish)
foods.source_notes: Shellfish allergen (tropomyosin). Cross-reacts with shrimp, crab, lobster. Histamine depends on freshness. Popular in Cajun cuisine.

foods.name: Mussels (Steamed)
foods.source_notes: Shellfish allergen (tropomyosin). Bivalve mollusk. Moderate histamine that increases rapidly with storage. Nickel from filter-feeding.

foods.name: Clams
foods.source_notes: Shellfish allergen. Bivalve mollusk. Can cross-react with other mollusks. Iron-rich. SIGHI 1.

foods.name: Scallops
foods.source_notes: Shellfish allergen (mollusk tropomyosin). Lower histamine than crustaceans when fresh. Quick cooking recommended. SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Cod (Fresh, Atlantic)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. Parvalbumin allergen (fish allergy). Low-histamine white fish. Good choice for HIT patients.

foods.name: Tilapia
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. White fish, low histamine. Fish allergen (parvalbumin). Mild flavor, commonly farm-raised.

foods.name: Catfish
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. Freshwater fish. Lower parvalbumin than cod. Often fried (adds gluten/oil concerns).

foods.name: Halibut
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. Large flatfish, low histamine. Fish allergen. Higher mercury than smaller fish.

foods.name: Swordfish
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Large predatory fish = higher histamine potential. Very high mercury. Fish allergen.

foods.name: Mahi Mahi
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Dolphinfish (not dolphin). Scombroid risk = moderate-high histamine if not handled properly. Fish allergen.

foods.name: Sardines (Fresh)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1 when truly fresh. Much less histamine than canned. Small oily fish degrade fast — freshness critical. Fish allergen.

foods.name: Anchovies (Fresh)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2 when fresh. Dramatically lower histamine than canned/cured. Small oily fish degrade quickly.

foods.name: Egg White (Cooked)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Primary egg allergen proteins: ovomucoid, ovalbumin, ovotransferrin. Cooking reduces but doesn't eliminate allergenicity. Most egg-allergic react to whites.

foods.name: Egg Yolk (Cooked)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Yolk allergen is alpha-livetin (Gal d 5). Less allergenic than white. Some egg-allergic patients tolerate yolk only. Rich in choline.

foods.name: McDonald's Egg McMuffin
foods.source_notes: English muffin (wheat/gluten), processed cheese (lactose), egg (allergen), Canadian bacon (moderate histamine). Contains soy lecithin.

foods.name: McDonald's Hash Browns
foods.source_notes: Potato, beef flavoring (contains wheat + milk derivatives), sodium acid pyrophosphate. Hidden allergens in 'natural beef flavor'.

foods.name: Starbucks Chai Tea Latte
foods.source_notes: Chai concentrate has cinnamon (very high salicylates), ginger, black tea. Steamed milk adds lactose. High sugar/fructose. DAO inhibitor from tea.

foods.name: Starbucks Matcha Latte
foods.source_notes: Matcha powder + sugar blend + steamed milk. Very high oxalates from matcha. DAO inhibitor (catechins). Milk allergen/lactose.

foods.name: Chipotle Carnitas Bowl
foods.source_notes: Slow-braised pork (moderate histamine from cooking time). Rice + beans (low FODMAPs). Salsa adds salicylates. Sour cream adds lactose if chosen.

foods.name: Chipotle Steak Bowl
foods.source_notes: Grilled steak (less histamine than braised carnitas). Chipotle adobo marinade has chili (salicylates). GF without tortilla.

foods.name: Subway Turkey Breast Sub
foods.source_notes: Deli turkey (high histamine/amines from processing), wheat bread (gluten + FODMAP fructans). Subway bread contains azodicarbonamide and soy.

foods.name: Taco Bell Mexican Pizza
foods.source_notes: Fried flour tortillas (wheat), seasoned beef, beans (GOS/lectins), pizza sauce (histamine/salicylates), cheese blend (lactose). Multi-allergen item.

foods.name: Wendy's Spicy Chicken Sandwich
foods.source_notes: Breaded (wheat/gluten), spicy seasoning (salicylates from cayenne), mayo (egg), bun (wheat FODMAP). Contains milk, soy, egg.

foods.name: Wendy's Frosty (Chocolate)
foods.source_notes: Milk-based frozen dessert with cocoa. High lactose, HFCS (fructose). Cocoa = DAO inhibitor + oxalates. Contains milk and soy.

foods.name: Chick-fil-A Nuggets (8-count)
foods.source_notes: Pressure-cooked in peanut oil (refined, lower allergen but still peanut-derived). Breading = wheat/gluten + milk powder. Contains egg in batter.

foods.name: Chick-fil-A Grilled Nuggets
foods.source_notes: Grilled chicken with seasoning. Much lower allergen load than breaded. No wheat/gluten/egg. Contains soy (soybean oil in marinade). One of safer fast food options.

foods.name: Panera Autumn Squash Soup
foods.source_notes: Butternut squash, cream, onion (fructans). Contains milk. Relatively clean ingredient list vs most fast food.

foods.name: Panera Caesar Salad
foods.source_notes: Caesar dressing = anchovies (high histamine) + parmesan (aged cheese = high histamine). Croutons = gluten. Contains egg, milk, fish, wheat, soy.

foods.name: Popeyes Chicken Sandwich
foods.source_notes: Buttermilk-battered (wheat + milk), spicy mayo (egg), pickles (moderate histamine). Contains wheat, milk, egg, soy. Cajun spice = salicylates.

foods.name: Chipotle Chips and Guacamole
foods.source_notes: Corn chips (GF), avocado (low histamine but some report as MCAS trigger), cilantro, lime (salicylates), jalapeño. Relatively clean fast food option.

foods.name: Starbucks Bacon Gouda Sandwich
foods.source_notes: Bacon (high histamine) + aged gouda (high histamine) + egg on wheat bun. Double-hit histamine food. Contains wheat, milk, egg, soy.

foods.name: Starbucks Egg Bites (Bacon Gruyere)
foods.source_notes: Sous vide eggs + bacon (high histamine) + gruyère (very high histamine aged cheese). GF but high-histamine. Contains milk, egg.

foods.name: Peanut Butter Cups (Reese's)
foods.source_notes: Peanut allergen + milk allergen. Contains soy lecithin. Cocoa = oxalates. HFCS = fructose. Cross-contact risk with tree nuts.

foods.name: Shrimp Cocktail
foods.source_notes: Shellfish allergen. Cocktail sauce = horseradish (salicylates) + tomato (histamine liberator). Often sulfite-preserved. Histamine depends on freshness.

foods.name: Whey Protein Concentrate
foods.source_notes: Milk allergen (whey fraction). Concentrate retains more lactose than isolate. Common allergen in fitness supplements.

foods.name: Ice Cream (Vanilla, Commercial)
foods.source_notes: Milk allergen + high lactose. Contains egg in many commercial brands. HFCS adds fructose. Sorbitol/guar gum in low-fat versions = polyols.

foods.name: Butter (Salted)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Milk fat = trace casein. Very low lactose (mostly removed in churning). Milk allergen technically present but many milk-allergic tolerate butter.

foods.name: String Cheese (Mozzarella)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Low-moisture part-skim mozzarella. Low histamine (not aged). Less lactose than soft cheeses. Common kids' snack.

foods.name: American Cheese (Processed)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1. Processed cheese product. Lower histamine than aged cheeses. Contains emulsifiers, sodium phosphate. Milk allergen.

foods.name: Panda Express Chow Mein
foods.source_notes: Wheat noodles (gluten), soy sauce (histamine + soy + wheat), sesame oil, onion/celery (fructans). Contains wheat, soy, sesame.

foods.name: Taco Bell Quesadilla (Cheese)
foods.source_notes: Flour tortilla (wheat/gluten), three-cheese blend (milk/lactose), jalapeño sauce. Contains wheat, milk, soy.

foods.name: Sweet Corn (Fresh, on Cob)
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP at half cob. GOS and polyols (sorbitol) increase at larger servings. Not a common allergen.

foods.name: Green Beans
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP at standard serving. Technically a legume but lower lectin than dried beans. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Romaine Lettuce
foods.source_notes: Monash green (low FODMAP). SIGHI 0. Very well tolerated. One of the safest foods for elimination diets.

foods.name: Iceberg Lettuce
foods.source_notes: Monash green. SIGHI 0. Even safer than romaine — virtually no triggers. Commonly used in elimination diet protocols.

foods.name: Cabbage (Green, Cooked)
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP at 1 cup. SIGHI 0. Cooking reduces FODMAP load. Cruciferous = gas-producing but not high FODMAP.

foods.name: Parsnip
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP polyols (mannitol) at larger serving. Moderate salicylates (RPAH). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Turnip
foods.source_notes: Monash green. SIGHI 0. Well-tolerated root vegetable. Good potato substitute on elimination diets.

foods.name: Granny Smith Apple
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP fructose + sorbitol. SIGHI 0. OAS cross-reaction with birch pollen. Less fructose than sweeter varieties.

foods.name: Nectarine
foods.source_notes: Monash high FODMAP polyols (sorbitol). SIGHI 0. Stone fruit with high sorbitol. OAS cross-reaction with birch pollen.

foods.name: Coconut (Fresh Meat)
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP at small serving. FDA classifies coconut as tree nut for allergen labeling (despite being a drupe). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Lime
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1 (histamine liberator, citrus). Moderate salicylates. Monash low FODMAP in juice amounts. Common ingredient in many cuisines.

foods.name: Jasmine Rice
foods.source_notes: Monash green. SIGHI 0. Low FODMAP. One of the safest grains for all protocols. Arsenic concern with frequent consumption.

foods.name: Arborio Rice
foods.source_notes: Short-grain Italian rice for risotto. Monash green. SIGHI 0. GF. High starch (resistant starch when cooled).

foods.name: Pasta (Gluten-Free, Rice-Based)
foods.source_notes: Monash green. Brown rice pasta slightly higher in lectins. GF but check for corn or soy additives. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Tortilla Chips (Corn)
foods.source_notes: Corn, oil, salt. GF (check for wheat cross-contact). Low FODMAP. SIGHI 0. May contain lime (salicylates in flavored varieties).

foods.name: Honey
foods.source_notes: Monash very high FODMAP fructose (excess fructose). SIGHI 0 histamine. RPAH moderate salicylates. Common sweetener but FODMAP disaster.

foods.name: Maple Syrup (Pure)
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP in small serving (mostly sucrose, not excess fructose). RPAH moderate salicylates. SIGHI 0. Better sweetener choice than honey for FODMAP.

foods.name: Brown Sugar
foods.source_notes: Sucrose + molasses. Low FODMAP in small amounts. RPAH low salicylates from molasses. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: White Sugar (Granulated)
foods.source_notes: Pure sucrose. Monash low FODMAP (equal glucose:fructose ratio). SIGHI 0. RPAH allowed. One of the safest sweeteners for elimination diets.

foods.name: Agave Nectar
foods.source_notes: ~85% fructose. Monash very high FODMAP. Marketed as healthy but worse than HFCS for fructose malabsorption. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Sriracha Sauce
foods.source_notes: Chili + garlic (fructans) + vinegar (histamine) + sugar. Very high salicylates from chili peppers. SIGHI 1-2.

foods.name: Soy Sauce (Regular, Kikkoman)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2-3. Fermented soy + wheat. High histamine and amines. Contains gluten (wheat). Soy allergen. Triple allergen: soy + wheat + histamine.

foods.name: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
foods.source_notes: Rice cakes (GF base) in gochujang sauce (fermented chili = histamine + salicylates). Often contains fish cake (wheat + fish). Popular Korean street food.

foods.name: Sundubu-jjigae (Soft Tofu Stew)
foods.source_notes: Silken tofu (soy/GOS) + gochugaru chili (salicylates) + often contains shellfish or anchovy broth (histamine). Soy allergen. Egg often added.

foods.name: Kimbap (Korean Rice Roll)
foods.source_notes: Rice + seaweed (nickel) + various fillings: ham (histamine), pickled radish, egg. Sesame oil. Less histamine than sushi (no raw fish). Contains sesame, egg.

foods.name: Onigiri (Rice Ball)
foods.source_notes: Plain rice + nori (seaweed = nickel). Filling varies: umeboshi (salicylates), salmon (fish allergen, histamine), tuna-mayo (high histamine). Profile is for plain/salmon.

foods.name: Yakitori (Grilled Chicken Skewers)
foods.source_notes: Grilled chicken with tare sauce (soy sauce + mirin + sugar). Soy sauce adds gluten + histamine. Shio (salt) version is lower risk. Fresh-grilled = lower histamine.

foods.name: Ramen (Tonkotsu Pork Broth)
foods.source_notes: 12-18hr pork bone broth = very high histamine. Wheat noodles (gluten). Soy sauce tare. Chashu pork (braised = histamine). Nori, menma (fermented bamboo). Multi-trigger bowl.

foods.name: Soba Noodles (Buckwheat)
foods.source_notes: Buckwheat is GF but most soba contains wheat flour (check ratio). Buckwheat itself is a significant allergen in Japan/Korea. High oxalates. Monash moderate FODMAP fructans.

foods.name: Churros
foods.source_notes: Fried wheat dough (gluten + FODMAP fructans) rolled in cinnamon-sugar (very high salicylates from cinnamon). Contains egg, wheat, sometimes milk.

foods.name: Mole Negro (Oaxacan)
foods.source_notes: Complex sauce: chocolate (oxalates, DAO inhibitor) + multiple dried chilies (salicylates) + spices + onion/garlic (fructans). 20+ ingredients. Very high salicylate load.

foods.name: Pozole (Hominy Stew)
foods.source_notes: Hominy corn + pork (histamine from long simmer). Dried chili base (salicylates). GF. Toppings: radish, cabbage, lime add salicylates.

foods.name: Horchata (Rice Drink)
foods.source_notes: Rice + cinnamon + sugar + vanilla. Cinnamon = high salicylates. Dairy-free. Some versions use condensed milk (add lactose). SIGHI 0 (when no milk).

foods.name: Aloo Gobi (Potato Cauliflower)
foods.source_notes: Potato + cauliflower + turmeric/cumin/coriander spice blend. Spice blend adds salicylates. Cauliflower moderate FODMAP polyols at large serving. Often contains garlic/onion (fructans).

foods.name: Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)
foods.source_notes: Tandoori chicken in tomato-cream-butter sauce. Tomato = histamine liberator. Cream = lactose. Onion/garlic/ginger = fructans. Kashmiri chili + spices = salicylates. Milk allergen.

foods.name: Masala Dosa
foods.source_notes: Fermented rice/lentil crepe (histamine from fermentation + lentil GOS/lectins) filled with spiced potato. Onion/mustard seeds in filling. Served with sambar (more fermented). GF.

foods.name: Pani Puri (Golgappa/Chaat)
foods.source_notes: Fried wheat/semolina puri (gluten) + chickpea (GOS/lectins) + tamarind-mint water (high salicylates). Street food chaat. Contains wheat. Mint and tamarind very high salicylates.

foods.name: Shawarma (Chicken)
foods.source_notes: Marinated chicken on vertical spit. Pita bread (wheat/gluten). Garlic sauce (fructans). Pickled turnip (histamine). Spice blend (salicylates). Tahini = sesame allergen.

foods.name: Fattoush Salad
foods.source_notes: Fried pita chips (wheat/gluten) + vegetables + sumac dressing (very high salicylates). Pomegranate molasses = moderate salicylates. Refreshing but sumac is an MCAS risk.

foods.name: Muhammara (Red Pepper Walnut Dip)
foods.source_notes: Roasted red peppers (salicylates) + walnuts (tree nut allergen, oxalates) + pomegranate molasses + Aleppo pepper. Breadcrumbs add gluten. Tree nut allergen.

foods.name: Manakeesh (Za'atar Flatbread)
foods.source_notes: Wheat flatbread (gluten + FODMAP fructans) topped with za'atar (thyme + sumac + sesame = high salicylates). Contains wheat, sesame. Sesame allergen (new Top-9).

foods.name: Trader Joe's Cauliflower Gnocchi
foods.source_notes: Cauliflower + potato starch + cassava flour. GF. Cauliflower = moderate FODMAP polyols at this serving. Popular GF option.

foods.name: KIND Bar (Nuts & Spices)
foods.source_notes: Almonds, peanuts, walnuts (tree nut + peanut allergens). Honey (fructose). Spice adds salicylates. Contains multiple allergens. GF.

foods.name: Siggi's Skyr (Plain)
foods.source_notes: Icelandic strained yogurt. Extended straining removes more lactose + whey than Greek yogurt. Fermented = moderate histamine. Milk allergen.

foods.name: Oatly Oat Milk (Original)
foods.source_notes: Oats are GF by nature but cross-contamination common. Oatly uses 'oat-safe' supply chain. Low FODMAP in standard serving. Contains rapeseed oil. Added B12/D.

foods.name: Larabar (Peanut Butter Cookie)
foods.source_notes: Dates (very high FODMAP fructose) + peanuts + sea salt. Simple ingredients but date base = FODMAP bomb. Peanut allergen. GF.

foods.name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich
foods.source_notes: Wheat bread (gluten + FODMAP fructans) + American/cheddar cheese (lactose) + butter. Contains wheat, milk. Simple but multi-allergen.

foods.name: PB&J Sandwich
foods.source_notes: Wheat bread (gluten + fructans) + peanut butter (peanut allergen) + grape/strawberry jelly (fructose + salicylates). Multi-allergen American staple.

foods.name: BLT Sandwich
foods.source_notes: Bacon (high histamine/amines) + lettuce + tomato (histamine liberator + salicylates) + mayo (egg) on wheat bread (gluten). Contains wheat, egg.

foods.name: Chicken Soup (Homemade)
foods.source_notes: Histamine depends on simmer time. Onion/garlic = fructans. If noodles added = gluten. Fresh-made short-simmer is lower histamine than long-simmered.

foods.name: Tuna Salad
foods.source_notes: Canned tuna (very high histamine) + mayo (egg) + celery/onion (fructans). SIGHI 3 from canned fish. Contains fish, egg. One of highest-histamine common foods.

foods.name: Egg Salad
foods.source_notes: Eggs + mayo (more egg) + celery/onion (fructans). SIGHI 0 for egg itself. Egg allergen. Lower histamine alternative to tuna salad.

foods.name: Chicken Caesar Wrap
foods.source_notes: Flour tortilla (wheat/gluten) + chicken + Caesar dressing (anchovies = high histamine, parmesan = high histamine, egg = allergen). Contains wheat, fish, egg, milk, soy.

foods.name: Oatmeal Cookie
foods.source_notes: Oats (cross-contaminated with wheat usually) + wheat flour + butter (milk) + sugar + cinnamon (salicylates) + raisins (salicylates). Contains wheat, milk, egg, soy.

foods.name: Banana Bread
foods.source_notes: Ripe bananas (amines increase with ripeness + high fructose when very ripe) + wheat flour (gluten) + egg + butter (milk). Contains wheat, egg, milk.

foods.name: Pho (Vietnamese Beef Noodle Soup)
foods.source_notes: Long-simmered beef bone broth (6-12hr = high histamine). Rice noodles (GF). Star anise + cinnamon (salicylates). Fish sauce (very high histamine). Hoisin + sriracha condiments add more.

foods.name: Banh Mi (Vietnamese Sandwich)
foods.source_notes: French baguette (wheat/gluten) + pâté (very high histamine liver product) + deli pork (histamine) + pickled daikon/carrots (vinegar = histamine) + cilantro + jalapeño (salicylates). Multi-trigger sandwich.

foods.name: Pad Thai
foods.source_notes: Rice noodles (GF) + tamarind + fish sauce (high histamine) + shrimp (shellfish allergen) + peanuts (peanut allergen) + egg. Contains shellfish, peanut, egg, fish. GF.

foods.name: Green Curry (Thai)
foods.source_notes: Green chili paste (salicylates) + coconut milk + fish sauce (histamine) + galangal + lemongrass + garlic/shallots (fructans). Contains fish. GF.

foods.name: Empanada (Beef)
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour dough (gluten + fructans) + ground beef + onion (fructans) + cumin/paprika (salicylates). Contains wheat, may contain egg.

foods.name: Grapefruit (Whole)

drug_interactions.interaction: Inhibits CYP3A4 enzyme, increasing drug bioavailability up to 5x. Risk of rhabdomyolysis.
CYP3A4 inhibition increases hypotensive effect.
CYP3A4 inhibition raises drug levels to toxic range.
Variable — may increase or decrease INR.
Mild CYP3A4 effect, may increase serotonergic effects.
Reduces absorption via OATP inhibition (opposite of other grapefruit interactions — decreases drug levels).

foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1 (histamine liberator, citrus). Furanocoumarins (bergamottin, 6',7'-DHB) irreversibly inhibit CYP3A4. Effect persists 24-72hr after single glass of juice.

foods.name: Kale (Raw, Large Serving)

drug_interactions.interaction: Very high vitamin K content (>500mcg per cup raw) directly antagonizes warfarin. Can cause sub-therapeutic INR.
Goitrogens in raw cruciferous may reduce thyroid function. Cook to reduce.

foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Very high vitamin K. High oxalates. Moderate nickel (soil uptake). Goitrogen when raw. Cruciferous = ITC compounds with anti-cancer properties.

foods.name: Aged Cheese (Generic, Tyramine-Rich)

drug_interactions.interaction: Tyramine not metabolized by MAO → hypertensive crisis ('cheese reaction'). Can be fatal.
Weak MAOI activity; tyramine interaction possible.

foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Generic entry for all aged cheeses (cheddar, gruyère, parmesan, stilton, etc.) as drug interaction reference. Tyramine 200-1200 mg/kg.

foods.name: Fermented Soy Products (Generic, Tyramine-Rich)

drug_interactions.interaction: Tyramine in miso, soy sauce, natto, tempeh → hypertensive crisis risk.
Weak MAOI activity; avoid large servings of fermented soy.

foods.source_notes: SIGHI 3. Reference entry for miso, natto, soy sauce, doenjang as MAOI interaction. Soy allergen. Tyramine 50-900 mg/kg depending on fermentation.

foods.name: Licorice Root (Real, Not Anise-Flavored)

drug_interactions.interaction: Glycyrrhizin inhibits 11β-HSD2, causing pseudoaldosteronism: sodium retention, potassium loss, hypertension.
Additive potassium loss. Risk of hypokalemia and cardiac arrhythmia.
Hypokalemia from licorice increases digoxin toxicity risk.
Licorice potentiates cortisol by blocking its metabolism.
Case reports of increased INR with chronic licorice use.

foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Glycyrrhizin is the active compound. 50g/day of real licorice candy can cause clinically significant hypokalemia. Not a concern with anise-flavored candy.

foods.name: Cranberry Juice (Unsweetened)

drug_interactions.interaction: Multiple case reports of increased INR. Mechanism debated: salicylate content, CYP2C9 inhibition, or vitamin K displacement.
May inhibit CYP2C9 metabolism, increasing drug levels.

foods.source_notes: RPAH very high salicylates. High oxalates (kidney stone risk). Cranberry-warfarin interaction is well-documented in pharmacovigilance.

foods.name: Pomelo

drug_interactions.interaction: Contains furanocoumarins similar to grapefruit. Same CYP3A4 inhibition mechanism.
CYP3A4 inhibition. Less potent than grapefruit but clinically significant.

foods.source_notes: Citrus grandis. Related to grapefruit. Contains bergamottin and other furanocoumarins. Often overlooked by patients who avoid grapefruit.

foods.name: Seville (Bitter) Orange

drug_interactions.interaction: Contains furanocoumarins. CYP3A4 inhibition like grapefruit. Used in marmalade and some cocktails.
Bitter orange extract contains synephrine — additive cardiovascular effects with stimulant medications.

foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1 (citrus histamine liberator). Marmalade, Cointreau, some herbal supplements. Patients often don't realize this is a grapefruit-equivalent.

foods.name: Broccoli (Vitamin K source)

drug_interactions.interaction: High vitamin K (89mcg per cup cooked). Consistent intake recommended rather than avoidance.
Goitrogens (reduced by cooking). Clinical significance low at normal dietary intake.

foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Monash low FODMAP at small serving (fructans at large). Cruciferous. Vitamin K drug interaction is about consistency, not avoidance.

foods.name: Green Tea (Concentrated/Supplement)

drug_interactions.interaction: High vitamin K in green tea leaves. Concentrated supplements significantly affect INR.
OATP inhibition reduces nadolol absorption by ~85%. Well-documented.
Tannins and EGCG chelate non-heme iron, reducing absorption. Take 2hr apart.
Caffeine content. Avoid large amounts.

foods.source_notes: DAO inhibitor. Very high oxalates in concentrated form. Multiple clinically significant drug interactions especially as supplement.

foods.name: Infant Rice Cereal (Fortified)
foods.source_notes: First solid food for many infants. GF (pure rice). Iron-fortified. Arsenic concern in rice cereals — AAP now recommends variety. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Baby Oatmeal Cereal
foods.source_notes: Iron-fortified oat cereal. Cross-contamination with wheat possible (check label). AAP recommends as alternative to rice cereal. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Baby Food Puree (Sweet Potato)
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP polyols (mannitol) at larger serving. Baby serving is small. SIGHI 0. Common first food. Well-tolerated by most.

foods.name: Baby Food Puree (Banana)
foods.source_notes: Ripe banana puree. Monash moderate fructose at larger serving. Amines increase with ripeness. SIGHI 0 (unripe) to 1 (very ripe).

foods.name: Baby Food Puree (Pea)
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP GOS. Legume = lectin. Common early allergen introduction food. Green pea is a legume allergen.

foods.name: Puffs (Baby Snack, Rice/Corn)
foods.source_notes: Dissolvable rice/corn puffs (Happy Baby, Gerber). GF versions available. Very low trigger load. SIGHI 0. Common toddler snack.

foods.name: Toddler Yogurt Pouch
foods.source_notes: Yogurt + fruit + added sugar. Fermented = moderate histamine. Lactose + fructose. Milk allergen. Common toddler snack — parents should know allergen profile.

foods.name: BCAA Powder (Branched-Chain Amino Acids)
foods.source_notes: L-leucine, L-isoleucine, L-valine. Usually flavored with sucralose/stevia + citric acid (histamine liberator in some). Polyols from sweeteners. Check for artificial colors.

foods.name: Pre-Workout Powder (C4/Ghost/etc)
foods.source_notes: Caffeine (DAO inhibitor) + beta-alanine + citrulline. Artificial colors (mast cell trigger). Caffeine content 150-300mg = significant DAO inhibition. MCAS patients should avoid.

foods.name: Recovery Shake (Chocolate Protein + Banana)
foods.source_notes: Whey protein (milk allergen) + cocoa (DAO inhibitor, oxalates) + banana (amines when ripe). Common post-workout. Lactose from whey concentrate.

foods.name: Protein Pancake Mix
foods.source_notes: Usually wheat/oat flour + whey protein + egg. Contains wheat, milk, egg. Some GF versions use rice/oat flour. Check label.

foods.name: Chicken Wings (Buffalo)
foods.source_notes: Fried chicken (may have flour coating = gluten) + cayenne hot sauce (very high salicylates) + butter (milk). Blue cheese dressing adds aged cheese histamine.

foods.name: Meatball (Beef/Pork, Italian-Style)
foods.source_notes: Ground meat + breadcrumbs (wheat/gluten) + egg + parmesan (aged cheese = histamine) + garlic/onion (fructans) + milk. Contains wheat, egg, milk.

foods.name: Meatloaf
foods.source_notes: Ground beef + breadcrumbs (gluten) + egg + onion (fructans) + ketchup/tomato glaze (histamine + salicylates). Contains wheat, egg, milk.

foods.name: Macaroni and Cheese (Homemade)
foods.source_notes: Wheat pasta (gluten + FODMAP fructans) + cheese sauce (milk/lactose) + butter. Contains wheat, milk. Cheddar cheese adds some histamine.

foods.name: Coleslaw
foods.source_notes: Cabbage + carrot + mayo (egg) + vinegar (histamine). Contains egg. SIGHI 0-1 depending on dressing.

foods.name: Corn on the Cob (Buttered)
foods.source_notes: Corn + butter (trace milk). Monash low FODMAP at half cob. Corn is not a common allergen. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Baked Potato (Plain)
foods.source_notes: Monash green. SIGHI 0. Nightshade (solanine) but well-tolerated by most. Cooking destroys lectins. One of safest foods for elimination diets.

foods.name: Mashed Potatoes
foods.source_notes: Potato + butter (milk) + milk/cream (lactose). Contains milk. Plain potato is SIGHI 0 but added dairy brings FODMAP lactose.

foods.name: Instant Ramen (Maruchan/Top Ramen)
foods.source_notes: Wheat noodles (gluten) + seasoning packet with MSG (amines), soy sauce powder (histamine + soy), garlic/onion powder (fructans). Contains wheat, soy. TBHQ preservative.

foods.name: Protein Bar (Generic, Whey-Based)
foods.source_notes: Whey protein (milk allergen) + sugar alcohols (polyols — erythritol, maltitol) + chocolate coating (cocoa). Many contain soy lecithin, tree nuts, peanuts.

foods.name: Veggie Burger (Impossible/Beyond)
foods.source_notes: Pea protein (lectin) + coconut/sunflower oil + methylcellulose. Beyond: pea protein, rice protein, mung bean. Soy-free but pea is a legume allergen. GF.

foods.name: Hummus (Store-Bought)
foods.source_notes: Chickpeas (high FODMAP GOS, lectins) + tahini (sesame allergen) + garlic (fructans) + lemon. Monash high FODMAP. Sesame is now Top-9 allergen (FASTER Act 2023).

foods.name: Fish Tacos
foods.source_notes: Battered fish (may contain wheat) on corn tortilla + cabbage slaw + chipotle mayo (egg) + salsa (salicylates). Fish allergen. Histamine depends on fish freshness.

foods.name: Pulled Pork
foods.source_notes: Slow-smoked pork (6-12hr = histamine accumulation). BBQ sauce adds fructose (HFCS), vinegar (histamine), spices (salicylates). Smoked meats are higher histamine.

foods.name: Steak (Grilled, Medium-Rare)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh-cooked. Fresh steak cooked immediately = very low histamine. One of safest protein options for HIT/MCAS. Dry-aged steak would be much higher.

foods.name: Dry-Aged Steak
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 2-3. 21-45 day dry-aging dramatically increases histamine and tyramine. Enzymatic breakdown concentrates biogenic amines. Premium product but MCAS nightmare.

foods.name: Kombucha (Low-Sugar/Hard)
foods.source_notes: Extended fermentation (lower sugar = longer ferment = more histamine). Hard kombucha adds alcohol (DAO inhibitor). Tea base = oxalates. Double-hit for MCAS.

foods.name: Almond Milk (Unsweetened)
foods.source_notes: Tree nut allergen (almond). Monash low FODMAP in standard serving. SIGHI 0. Low oxalates (diluted). Commonly fortified with calcium + D. No lactose.

foods.name: Coconut Milk (Carton, Drinking)
foods.source_notes: Diluted coconut cream. Very low allergen load. FDA classifies coconut as tree nut. Monash low FODMAP. SIGHI 0. Good dairy alternative for HIT patients.

foods.name: Cashew Milk
foods.source_notes: Tree nut allergen (cashew). Diluted = lower GOS than whole cashews. Monash low FODMAP at standard serving. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Cornbread
foods.source_notes: Cornmeal + flour (often wheat blend — check recipe) + milk + egg + butter. Contains milk, egg, often wheat. Some recipes are GF (cornmeal only).

foods.name: Waffles (Homemade)
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour (gluten + fructans) + egg + milk (lactose) + butter. Contains wheat, milk, egg. Toppings add: maple syrup (salicylates), fruit (varies).

foods.name: Croissant
foods.source_notes: Laminated wheat dough (very high gluten) + butter (milk). High FODMAP fructans from wheat. Contains wheat, milk, egg. Luxurious but multi-allergen.

foods.name: Biscuit (Southern-Style)
foods.source_notes: All-purpose flour + butter + buttermilk. Very high gluten from soft wheat flour. Contains wheat, milk. Buttermilk adds lactose.

foods.name: Chocolate Chip Cookie
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour (gluten) + butter (milk) + egg + chocolate (oxalates, DAO inhibitor) + sugar. Contains wheat, milk, egg, soy (in chocolate). Multi-allergen.

foods.name: Brownie
foods.source_notes: High cocoa content = high oxalates + DAO inhibitor. Wheat flour (gluten, less than cookies due to cocoa ratio). Contains wheat, milk, egg, soy. Cocoa is the main concern.

foods.name: Cheesecake
foods.source_notes: Cream cheese (fresh = low histamine but high lactose) + sugar + eggs + graham cracker crust (wheat). Contains milk, egg, wheat. Very high lactose from cream cheese + sour cream.

foods.name: Ethiopian Doro Wat (Chicken Stew)
foods.source_notes: Chicken stewed in berbere spice (very high salicylates from multiple chilies + spices) + onions (very high fructans — Ethiopian recipes use massive amounts). Eggs often added. Served with injera (fermented = histamine). GF.

foods.name: Pupusa (Cheese/Bean, Salvadoran)
foods.source_notes: Corn masa (GF) filled with cheese (milk/lactose) + refried beans (GOS/lectins). Curtido (fermented cabbage topping) adds histamine. Contains milk. GF.

foods.name: Arepa (Corn, Colombian/Venezuelan)
foods.source_notes: Pre-cooked corn flour (P.A.N.) + water + salt. Plain arepa is very well tolerated — GF, low FODMAP, SIGHI 0. Fillings change profile dramatically (cheese = lactose, meat = varies).

foods.name: Bibimbap (with Gochujang)
foods.source_notes: Rice + vegetables + egg + gochujang (fermented chili paste = histamine + salicylates). Sesame oil (sesame allergen). Contains egg, sesame, soy (gochujang has soy). GF if no wheat-based gochujang.

foods.name: Turkey Burger
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh-ground and immediately cooked. No bun = GF. Lower fat than beef. Good HIT-safe protein option.

foods.name: Chicken Salad (Rotisserie-Based)
foods.source_notes: Rotisserie chicken (moderate histamine from display time) + mayo (egg) + celery/onion (fructans). Contains egg. Histamine increases with how long the chicken sat in display.

foods.name: Spaghetti Bolognese
foods.source_notes: Wheat pasta (gluten + fructans) + tomato sauce (histamine + salicylates + lectins) + ground beef + onion/garlic (fructans) + wine (histamine). Multi-trigger classic. Contains wheat.

foods.name: Lasagna
foods.source_notes: Pasta sheets (wheat) + bolognese sauce (tomato histamine) + béchamel (milk/lactose) + parmesan (aged cheese histamine) + ricotta (lactose). Contains wheat, milk, egg. Maximum trigger density.

foods.name: Cobb Salad
foods.source_notes: Chicken + bacon (high histamine) + blue cheese (very high histamine) + hard-boiled egg + avocado + tomato (histamine liberator). Despite being a 'salad', very high histamine from bacon + blue cheese combo.

foods.name: Club Sandwich
foods.source_notes: Triple-decker toast (wheat/gluten) + deli turkey (high histamine) + bacon (high histamine) + tomato (histamine liberator) + mayo (egg). Contains wheat, egg.

foods.name: Protein Smoothie Bowl (Acai Base)
foods.source_notes: Acai (high salicylates) + banana (amines) + granola (may contain tree nuts, wheat) + honey (fructose). Common toppings add allergens. Looks healthy but high salicylate + fructose.

foods.name: Rotisserie Chicken (Whole)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1-2. Store display = histamine accumulation. Seasoning varies. Better than deli meat but worse than home-cooked. Eat same day.

foods.name: Grilled Chicken Breast (Restaurant)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0-1. Restaurant-grilled is usually lower histamine than store-bought. Check for soy/wheat in marinades. One of safest restaurant protein options.

foods.name: Fried Egg (Over Easy/Sunny Side Up)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Fresh egg cooked in butter/oil. Egg allergen. Very low trigger load otherwise. MCAS-friendly protein.

foods.name: Hard-Boiled Egg
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Egg allergen. Cooking fully denatures some allergen proteins. Portable protein. HIT-safe.

foods.name: Omelet (Cheese and Vegetable)
foods.source_notes: Eggs + cheese (lactose, mild histamine if not aged) + bell pepper/onion (fructans). Contains egg, milk. Profile varies significantly by cheese type and vegetables.

foods.name: Clementine (Mandarin Orange)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 1 (citrus = histamine liberator). Moderate salicylates. Fructose moderate at >2 fruits. Less acidic than oranges.

foods.name: Cherries (Sweet, Fresh)
foods.source_notes: Monash high FODMAP polyols (sorbitol). RPAH high salicylates. SIGHI 0 histamine. OAS cross-reaction with birch pollen. Stone fruit.

foods.name: Cranberries (Fresh)
foods.source_notes: RPAH very high salicylates. Moderate oxalates. SIGHI 0 histamine. Fresh cranberries are low FODMAP (vs dried which have added sugar/fructose).

foods.name: Butternut Squash
foods.source_notes: Monash low FODMAP at standard serving. SIGHI 0. Well-tolerated winter squash. Good carb source on elimination diets.

foods.name: Zucchini (Cooked)
foods.source_notes: Monash green. SIGHI 0. Very well-tolerated. Popular zoodle/noodle substitute. Low in everything.

foods.name: Spaghetti Squash
foods.source_notes: Monash green. SIGHI 0. GF pasta alternative. Extremely well-tolerated. Elimination diet staple.

foods.name: Chipotle Queso Blanco
foods.source_notes: White cheese dip with jalapeños (salicylates). Contains milk. GF. Fresher cheese = lower histamine than aged versions.

foods.name: Wingstop Wings (Lemon Pepper)
foods.source_notes: Fried wings (may have flour coating) + lemon pepper seasoning (citric acid = histamine liberator, pepper = salicylates) + butter (milk). Contains milk.

foods.name: Sweetgreen Harvest Bowl
foods.source_notes: Wild rice + roasted chicken + sweet potato + goat cheese + apples. Cleaner ingredient list. Goat cheese is low-histamine. Contains milk. GF.

foods.name: Greek Yogurt Parfait (Commercial)
foods.source_notes: Greek yogurt (fermented = histamine) + granola (wheat/gluten, tree nuts) + honey (fructose) + berries (salicylates). Contains milk, wheat, tree nuts.

foods.name: Rice Krispies Treat
foods.source_notes: Rice cereal (may contain malt extract = gluten) + marshmallow (corn syrup, gelatin) + butter (milk). Contains milk. Some brands GF.

foods.name: Pop-Tarts (Strawberry)
foods.source_notes: Wheat pastry (gluten + fructans) + strawberry filling (HFCS = fructose, artificial color = salicylates). Contains wheat, soy. Artificial Red 40.

foods.name: Falafel Wrap (Pita)
foods.source_notes: Chickpea falafel (high GOS + lectins) in pita (wheat/gluten + fructans) + tahini (sesame allergen) + pickled turnip (histamine). Contains wheat, sesame. Very high FODMAP.

foods.name: Tacos Al Pastor
foods.source_notes: Marinated pork (achiote + chili = salicylates) on corn tortilla (GF) + pineapple (histamine liberator) + onion/cilantro. Vertical spit cooking = moderate histamine from display time.

foods.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
foods.source_notes: Yogurt-marinated chicken (fermented = histamine) in tomato-cream sauce (histamine liberator + lactose). Onion/garlic (fructans) + spice blend (salicylates). Contains milk.

foods.name: Spring Rolls (Fresh, Vietnamese)
foods.source_notes: Rice paper (GF) + fresh vegetables + shrimp or chicken + herbs. Relatively low trigger load. Dipping sauce (nuoc cham = fish sauce = high histamine) changes profile significantly. Contains shellfish or fish.

foods.name: Curry Laksa (Malaysian)
foods.source_notes: Coconut milk curry broth + shrimp paste (very high histamine) + wheat/rice noodles + chili paste (salicylates). Contains shellfish, fish, wheat (if wheat noodles). Shrimp paste is the histamine driver.

foods.name: Mascarpone
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Fresh cream cheese (not aged). Low histamine. High fat. Moderate lactose. Milk allergen. Used in tiramisu.

foods.name: Burrata
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0. Fresh mozzarella shell filled with stracciatella cream. Not aged = very low histamine. Higher lactose than aged cheeses. Milk allergen. HIT-friendly cheese option.

foods.name: Popcorn (Movie Theater, Buttered)
foods.source_notes: Corn + coconut oil (or butter flavoring containing milk). Movie theater butter topping often contains diacetyl + milk derivatives. Plain air-popped is SIGHI 0, GF, low FODMAP.

foods.name: Tortilla Chips (Flavored, Doritos-Style)
foods.source_notes: Corn chips + seasoning: cheese powder (milk/lactose), onion/garlic powder (fructans), paprika/chili (salicylates), MSG. Contains milk, soy. More complex than plain chips.

foods.name: Granola Bar (Nature Valley Oats 'n Honey)
foods.source_notes: Oats (may contain wheat cross-contact) + honey (very high fructose) + sugar + canola oil. Contains wheat. Fructans from oats/wheat.

foods.name: Ground Turkey
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. Cook same day as purchase. Good HIT-safe protein. Lean option.

foods.name: Lamb Chops (Fresh)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. Lamb is rarely allergenic. Higher in amines if aged/marinated. One of safest red meat options for elimination diets.

foods.name: Pork Chops (Fresh)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. Fresh pork is low histamine. Dramatically different from cured/processed pork products. Cook same day.

foods.name: Sea Bass (Fresh)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0 when fresh. White fish, low histamine. Fish allergen (parvalbumin). Good HIT-safe fish option if truly fresh.

foods.name: Shrimp (Fresh, Cooked Immediately)
foods.source_notes: SIGHI 0-1 when truly fresh. Shellfish allergen (tropomyosin). Fresh-caught and immediately cooked = much lower histamine than thawed frozen. Histamine liberator in some individuals.

foods.name: Sloppy Joe
foods.source_notes: Ground beef + tomato sauce (histamine + salicylates) + ketchup (HFCS + tomato) + onion/green pepper (fructans) on wheat bun (gluten). Contains wheat.

foods.name: Shepherd's Pie
foods.source_notes: Ground lamb/beef + onion/carrot/peas (fructans) + mashed potato topping (milk/lactose). Contains milk. GF if no flour thickener. Relatively moderate trigger load for a complete meal.

foods.name: Chili Con Carne
foods.source_notes: Ground beef + beans (high GOS/lectins) + tomato (histamine) + chili powder (very high salicylates) + onion/garlic (fructans). Long simmer = histamine. GF. Multi-FODMAP + salicylate bomb.

foods.name: Beef Stew
foods.source_notes: Beef + onion/carrot/potato + tomato paste (histamine) + flour thickener (gluten). Long simmer = histamine accumulation. GF if no flour. Contains wheat (usually).

foods.name: Chicken Pot Pie
foods.source_notes: Pie crust (wheat/gluten + butter/milk) + chicken + cream sauce (milk/lactose) + onion/celery (fructans) + peas. Contains wheat, milk, egg. Classic comfort food, many triggers.

foods.name: Avocado Toast (Restaurant)
foods.source_notes: Sourdough/wheat bread (gluten + fructans) + avocado (polyols = sorbitol per Monash) + often topped with egg, chili flakes (salicylates), everything seasoning. Contains wheat, egg.

foods.name: Smoothie (Tropical, Mango/Pineapple)
foods.source_notes: Mango (high fructose when ripe) + pineapple (histamine liberator) + banana (amines) + coconut milk/juice. High FODMAP fructose from fruit concentration. Salicylates from tropical fruits.

foods.name: Almond Butter
foods.source_notes: Tree nut allergen (almond). Monash low FODMAP at 1 tbsp. SIGHI 0. Moderate oxalates. RPAH moderate salicylates. Common peanut butter alternative.

foods.name: Sunflower Seed Butter (SunButter)
foods.source_notes: Nut-free, soy-free, GF. Top-8 allergen free. Moderate nickel and oxalates. Common school-safe nut butter alternative. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Cauliflower Rice (Frozen)
foods.source_notes: Monash moderate FODMAP polyols (mannitol) at 1 cup. Popular rice substitute for low-carb/GF. SIGHI 0. Smaller serving = low FODMAP.

foods.name: Fish and Chips
foods.source_notes: Battered fish (wheat/gluten + fish allergen) + fried potatoes. Histamine depends on fish freshness. Malt vinegar topping adds histamine + gluten. Contains wheat, fish, egg (in batter).

foods.name: Nachos (Loaded, Restaurant)
foods.source_notes: Corn chips (GF) + cheese (lactose) + beans (GOS/lectins) + jalapeños (salicylates) + sour cream (lactose) + guacamole + salsa (tomato = histamine). Multi-FODMAP. Contains milk.

foods.name: Stir-Fry (Chicken and Vegetable)
foods.source_notes: Chicken + broccoli/bell pepper + soy sauce (histamine + gluten + soy) + garlic (fructans) + ginger. Contains soy, wheat (soy sauce). Use coconut aminos for HIT-friendly version.

foods.name: Fried Rice (Takeout)
foods.source_notes: Rice + egg (allergen) + soy sauce (histamine + gluten + soy) + scallion/garlic (fructans) + sesame oil (sesame allergen). Contains egg, soy, wheat, sesame. Day-old rice used (resistant starch).

foods.name: Ham
foods.source_notes: Cured pork. Very high histamine due to curing/aging process. High amines (tyramine). Contains nitrates/nitrites. Major MCAS trigger. SIGHI 2-3. Monash low FODMAP.

foods.name: Veal
foods.source_notes: Fresh veal is low histamine when consumed promptly. Younger meat = less biogenic amine accumulation than aged beef. Monash low FODMAP. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Fig
foods.source_notes: High FODMAP (fructose, fructans). Monash red for fresh figs >1 medium. High salicylates per RPAH. Contains ficin (latex cross-reactivity). SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Date
foods.source_notes: Very high FODMAP (fructose + fructans). Monash red >1 date. High salicylates per RPAH. Alias for 'dates' general query. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Portobello Mushroom
foods.source_notes: High FODMAP polyols (mannitol). Monash red for >75g. Mature cremini variant. SIGHI 0-1. Low histamine when fresh.

foods.name: Penne
foods.source_notes: Wheat pasta. Very high gluten, high fructans per Monash (red >1 cup cooked). High nickel. Similar to Pasta (White) but specific shape alias. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Sprite
foods.source_notes: Lemon-lime carbonated soft drink. High fructose corn syrup (high FODMAP fructose in excess of glucose). Contains citric acid, natural flavors. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Olive Garden Fettuccine Alfredo
foods.source_notes: Wheat fettuccine + heavy cream + Parmesan (aged cheese = histamine, amines) + butter + garlic (fructans). Contains wheat, milk, egg. Very high gluten and lactose. SIGHI 1-2 due to aged cheese.

foods.name: Olive Garden Breadsticks
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour breadstick with butter and garlic salt. Very high gluten, high fructans. Contains wheat, milk. Monash red for wheat bread. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Raising Cane's Chicken Fingers
foods.source_notes: Breaded fried chicken tenders. Wheat flour batter, soybean oil. Contains wheat, soy. High gluten from batter. Cane's sauce contains mayo (egg), Worcestershire (fish), garlic (fructans). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Lucky Charms
foods.source_notes: Oat-based cereal with marshmallows. Contains oat flour (gluten via contamination), modified corn starch, sugar, gelatin (marshmallows). Contains wheat, oats. High in sugar. Artificial colors. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Special K
foods.source_notes: Rice and wheat flakes. Very high gluten (wheat). Contains wheat, soy, barley malt flavoring. Fortified with iron (nickel cross-reactor). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: M&Ms
foods.source_notes: Milk chocolate candy. Contains milk, soy lecithin. Peanut variety adds peanut allergen. Chocolate = moderate oxalates, amines, nickel. Artificial colors. SIGHI 1 (chocolate). Monash: chocolate low FODMAP in small serves.

foods.name: Kit Kat
foods.source_notes: Chocolate-covered wafer bar. Contains wheat (wafer), milk, soy lecithin. High gluten from wheat wafer. Chocolate contributes amines, oxalates, nickel. SIGHI 1 (chocolate).

foods.name: Twix
foods.source_notes: Chocolate, caramel, cookie bar. Contains wheat (cookie), milk (caramel + chocolate), soy lecithin. High gluten from wheat cookie base. SIGHI 1 (chocolate).

foods.name: Skittles
foods.source_notes: Fruit-flavored candy. Sugar, corn syrup, citric acid, artificial flavors/colors. No major allergens (gelatin-free since 2009). HFCS-derived fructose concern. SIGHI 0-1 (citric acid, artificial additives may trigger MCAS).

foods.name: Starburst
foods.source_notes: Fruit chew candy. Sugar, corn syrup, palm oil, citric acid, gelatin, artificial flavors. Contains gelatin. No top-8 allergens but gelatin = animal-derived. SIGHI 0-1 (citric acid, artificial additives).

foods.name: Vindaloo
foods.source_notes: Goan-Portuguese curry. Wine vinegar base (histamine + amines), garlic + onion (fructans), heavy spice blend (very high salicylates). Vinegar = SIGHI 2. Traditionally pork but commonly chicken/lamb in US. MCAS concern from vinegar + spices.

foods.name: Char Siu
foods.source_notes: Cantonese BBQ pork. Soy sauce (gluten, soy), hoisin (soy, wheat), honey, five-spice, red fermented bean curd (histamine, amines). Fermented bean curd = SIGHI 2. Contains soy, wheat.

foods.name: Doro Wat
foods.source_notes: Ethiopian chicken stew with berbere spice, onion, garlic, eggs. High fructans (onion/garlic). High salicylates (berbere spice blend). Contains eggs. Alias entry for common shortened search query. SIGHI 1.

foods.name: Tiramisu
foods.source_notes: Mascarpone (aged cheese = histamine), raw eggs, espresso (amines, oxalates), ladyfingers (wheat, eggs), cocoa powder (amines, nickel, oxalates), Marsala wine (histamine). Very high histamine load from multiple sources. SIGHI 3. Contains wheat, milk, eggs, alcohol.

foods.name: Red Velvet Cake
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour, buttermilk, cocoa powder, cream cheese frosting, eggs, butter, red food coloring. Contains wheat, milk, eggs. High gluten, high lactose from buttermilk + cream cheese frosting. Cocoa = amines/oxalates/nickel. Artificial colors may trigger MCAS. SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Jello
foods.source_notes: Gelatin, sugar, artificial flavors/colors, citric acid. Contains gelatin (animal-derived). Generally well-tolerated on elimination diets. Artificial colors/citric acid may trigger MCAS in sensitive individuals. SIGHI 0. Monash low FODMAP in standard serving.

foods.name: Congee
foods.source_notes: Plain rice porridge. Very well tolerated. Common recovery/elimination diet food. Low everything when plain. Toppings (century egg, pork floss, pickled vegetables) add histamine risk. SIGHI 0. Monash low FODMAP.

foods.name: Filet Mignon
foods.source_notes: Beef tenderloin cut. Low histamine when fresh. Increases rapidly with aging/storage. SIGHI 0 fresh, 2+ if aged. Monash low FODMAP. Iron-rich.

foods.name: Brisket
foods.source_notes: Slow-smoked/braised beef. Long cooking time = high histamine and tyramine development. BBQ rub spices may add salicylates. SIGHI 2-3 (slow-cooked). Major MCAS trigger due to extended cooking time.

foods.name: Chicken Tenders
foods.source_notes: Breaded fried chicken. Wheat flour batter = high gluten, moderate fructans. Fried in soybean oil (soy). Contains wheat, soy, possibly egg in batter. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Lychee
foods.source_notes: Tropical fruit. High fructose (Monash red >5 fruits). Moderate polyols (sorbitol). Moderate salicylates per RPAH. Potential latex cross-reactivity. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Passion Fruit
foods.source_notes: Tropical fruit. High salicylates per RPAH. Moderate fructose. Contains latex-related allergens (cross-reactivity with latex allergy). SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Persimmon
foods.source_notes: High tannin fruit. High salicylates per RPAH. Moderate polyols (sorbitol). Contains bezoar risk compounds. Monash tested: moderate FODMAP. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Dragon Fruit
foods.source_notes: Tropical cactus fruit. Moderate oxalates (in seeds). Generally well tolerated. Low histamine. Cross-reactivity with cactus/Caryophyllales plants. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Arugula
foods.source_notes: Cruciferous leafy green. High salicylates per RPAH. Moderate oxalates (higher than lettuce). Goitrogenic. Monash low FODMAP. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Bok Choy
foods.source_notes: Cruciferous vegetable (Brassica rapa). Moderate polyols (sorbitol) per Monash — green for 1 cup, amber for >1 cup. Moderate salicylates per RPAH. Goitrogenic. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Shiitake Mushroom
foods.source_notes: High FODMAP polyols (mannitol). Monash red for all serves. Contains lentinan (beta-glucan immune modulator — relevant to MCAS). Dried shiitake = even higher polyol concentration. SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: French Toast
foods.source_notes: Bread soaked in egg-milk mixture, pan-fried. Contains wheat, eggs, milk. Very high gluten, high fructans from bread. Lactose from milk. Often served with syrup (fructose). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Rice Noodles
foods.source_notes: Rice flour noodles. Gluten-free. Very well tolerated. Common in pho, pad thai, stir-fries. Monash low FODMAP. SIGHI 0. Safe for elimination diets.

foods.name: Cappuccino
foods.source_notes: Espresso + steamed milk foam. High lactose from milk (use lactose-free milk to reduce). Coffee = amines, salicylates, oxalates. DAO inhibitor. SIGHI 1 (coffee). Monash: milk limit applies.

foods.name: Root Beer
foods.source_notes: Carbonated soft drink. HFCS (high fructose). Sassafras/wintergreen/anise flavoring = moderate salicylates. Caramel color. Caffeine-free. SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Tomato Juice
foods.source_notes: Processed tomato product. High histamine (processed tomato). Very high salicylates per RPAH. High oxalates. Histamine liberator. SIGHI 2. Major MCAS trigger. Nightshade. Contains high sodium.

foods.name: Salsa
foods.source_notes: Tomato, onion, jalapeño, cilantro, lime. Very high salicylates (tomato + chili). High fructans (onion). Tomato = histamine, lectins, oxalates. Nightshade. SIGHI 1-2. MCAS trigger.

foods.name: Alfredo Sauce
foods.source_notes: Butter, heavy cream, Parmesan (aged cheese = histamine + amines), garlic (fructans). Very high lactose. Contains milk. SIGHI 1-2 (aged cheese). Often contains flour (gluten thickener).

foods.name: Marinara Sauce
foods.source_notes: Cooked tomato sauce with garlic, onion, basil, olive oil. High histamine (cooked tomato). Very high salicylates. High fructans (garlic + onion). Nightshade. SIGHI 2. Major MCAS trigger.

foods.name: Caesar Dressing
foods.source_notes: Contains anchovy (fish, high histamine + amines), Parmesan (aged cheese = histamine + amines), egg yolk, garlic (fructans), lemon. Contains fish, eggs, milk. SIGHI 2-3. Major MCAS trigger.

foods.name: Tartar Sauce
foods.source_notes: Mayonnaise-based (egg) with pickles (vinegar = histamine), capers, onion (fructans), lemon. Contains eggs. Pickles/vinegar = SIGHI 1-2. Moderate MCAS concern.

foods.name: Cocktail Sauce
foods.source_notes: Ketchup base (tomato = histamine, salicylates) + horseradish (salicylates, MCAS trigger) + lemon + Worcestershire (fish). Contains fish (Worcestershire). SIGHI 1-2. Nightshade.

foods.name: Chimichurri
foods.source_notes: Parsley, garlic, oregano, olive oil, red wine vinegar. Very high salicylates (parsley + oregano + olive oil). High fructans (garlic). Vinegar = histamine. SIGHI 1-2. MCAS trigger from herb + vinegar combination.

foods.name: Sushi Roll
foods.source_notes: Rice + raw fish (high histamine + amines) + nori + rice vinegar (histamine). Soy sauce for dipping (gluten, soy). Contains fish, soy, wheat (soy sauce). SIGHI 2-3 for raw fish. Major MCAS trigger. Wasabi = salicylate spike.

foods.name: California Roll
foods.source_notes: Imitation crab (surimi = shellfish allergen, wheat starch), avocado (amines, moderate histamine), cucumber, rice, nori, rice vinegar. Contains shellfish, wheat (surimi), soy (soy sauce). SIGHI 1 (no raw fish, lower than traditional sushi).

foods.name: Spicy Tuna Roll
foods.source_notes: Raw tuna (very high histamine + amines, scombroid risk), sriracha/chili (high salicylates), mayo (egg), rice, nori. Contains fish, egg, soy, wheat (soy sauce). SIGHI 3. Major MCAS trigger — one of highest histamine foods. Tuna = highest scombroid risk fish.

foods.name: General Tso's Chicken
foods.source_notes: Battered fried chicken in sweet-spicy sauce. Soy sauce (gluten + soy), wheat flour batter, garlic + ginger (fructans), chili (salicylates), sugar/HFCS (fructose), corn starch. Contains wheat, soy, egg. SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Kung Pao Chicken
foods.source_notes: Chicken with peanuts, dried chili, Sichuan peppercorn, soy sauce. Contains peanuts, soy, wheat (soy sauce). High salicylates (dried chili, Sichuan pepper). High fructans (garlic, green onion). SIGHI 0-1.

foods.name: Mapo Tofu
foods.source_notes: Silken tofu in spicy fermented bean sauce. Doubanjiang (fermented broad bean + chili = histamine + amines), soy sauce (gluten, soy), garlic (fructans), Sichuan pepper (salicylates), ground pork. Contains soy, wheat. Fermented sauce = SIGHI 2. GOS from soy. MCAS concern from fermented + spicy.

foods.name: Crème Brûlée
foods.source_notes: Heavy cream, egg yolks, sugar, vanilla. Contains milk, eggs. Very high lactose from heavy cream. Vanilla extract = salicylates. SIGHI 0. Relatively well tolerated aside from dairy.

foods.name: Gelato
foods.source_notes: Italian frozen dessert. More milk, less cream than ice cream. Very high lactose. Contains milk, eggs (some recipes). Monash: lactose issue. SIGHI 0. Flavor-dependent: chocolate adds amines/oxalates/nickel; pistachio adds tree nuts.

foods.name: Cupcake
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour, sugar, butter, eggs, milk, frosting (sugar, butter, cream cheese/buttercream). Contains wheat, milk, eggs. High gluten, high lactose from frosting. SIGHI 0. Artificial colors in frosting may trigger MCAS.

foods.name: Eggs Benedict
foods.source_notes: Poached eggs, Canadian bacon/ham (high histamine + amines), hollandaise (butter + egg yolk + lemon), English muffin (wheat). Contains wheat, eggs, milk. SIGHI 2-3 (cured meat + hollandaise). Major MCAS trigger.

foods.name: Quiche
foods.source_notes: Pie crust (wheat, butter), eggs, cream, cheese (Gruyère = aged = histamine/amines), often bacon/ham (cured meat = histamine). Contains wheat, milk, eggs. High gluten, high lactose. Lorraine variant = SIGHI 2 (aged cheese + cured meat). MCAS concern.

foods.name: Frittata
foods.source_notes: Eggs, vegetables (onion/garlic = fructans), cheese, olive oil. Contains eggs, milk. Gluten-free unless served on bread. Histamine depends on cheese used (aged = higher). SIGHI 0-1 depending on fillings.

foods.name: Clam Chowder
foods.source_notes: Clams (shellfish, high histamine/amines), cream/milk (high lactose), potatoes, onion/celery (fructans), flour roux (gluten). Contains shellfish, milk, wheat. SIGHI 2. Major allergen load: shellfish + dairy + wheat.

foods.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
foods.source_notes: Chicken broth (long-simmered = histamine development), egg noodles (wheat + egg), celery/onion/carrot (fructans). Contains wheat, eggs. Homemade with short cook time is lower histamine. Canned = SIGHI 2. Monash: onion is high FODMAP.

foods.name: Greek Salad
foods.source_notes: Tomato (histamine, salicylates, lectins, oxalates), cucumber, red onion (fructans), olives (histamine, amines), feta cheese (aged = histamine/amines), olive oil, oregano (salicylates). Nightshade. SIGHI 1-2 (olives + aged cheese). Gluten-free.

foods.name: Pop-Tarts
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour pastry with fruit/frosting filling. Contains wheat, soy. Very high gluten. HFCS (high fructose). Artificial colors/flavors may trigger MCAS. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Pringles
foods.source_notes: Dehydrated potato, wheat starch, corn starch, rice flour. Contains wheat. Not a typical chip — reformed/processed. Moderate gluten from wheat starch. Whey in some flavors (lactose). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Snickers
foods.source_notes: Peanuts, caramel, nougat, milk chocolate. Contains peanuts, milk, soy, egg. Chocolate = amines, oxalates, nickel. Peanuts = top-8 allergen + GOS. SIGHI 1 (chocolate).

foods.name: Hershey's Chocolate Bar
foods.source_notes: Milk chocolate bar. Contains milk, soy lecithin. Cocoa = high oxalates, moderate amines (theobromine, phenylethylamine), moderate nickel. SIGHI 1 (chocolate). Monash: chocolate low FODMAP in small serves.

foods.name: Apple Pie
foods.source_notes: Wheat flour crust (very high gluten), apples (fructose + sorbitol), sugar, butter (lactose), cinnamon (salicylates). Contains wheat, milk. Monash red for apple (sorbitol + fructose). SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Pumpkin Pie
foods.source_notes: Wheat crust, pumpkin purée, evaporated milk, eggs, pumpkin pie spice (cinnamon/ginger/nutmeg = salicylates). Contains wheat, milk, eggs. Very high gluten. Monash: pumpkin low FODMAP, but crust + milk add FODMAPs. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Pecan Pie
foods.source_notes: Wheat crust, pecans (tree nut allergen), corn syrup (high fructose), eggs, butter. Contains tree nuts, wheat, eggs, milk. Very high gluten. Tree nut allergy risk. SIGHI 0.

foods.name: Lentil Soup
foods.source_notes: Lentils (very high GOS per Monash, high lectins), onion/garlic (fructans), carrot, celery, cumin/turmeric (salicylates). Very high FODMAP. High nickel (lentils). SIGHI 0-1. Pressure-cooking reduces lectins significantly.

foods.name: Rice Pudding
foods.source_notes: Rice, milk, sugar, cinnamon/vanilla. Contains milk. Very high lactose. Gluten-free. Cinnamon = salicylates. Often made with raisins (high fructose, salicylates). SIGHI 0. Monash: lactose from milk is main FODMAP concern.
